title: TCS To Acquire Porsche's IT Consulting Arm MHP for $373 Million
excerpt: India's largest IT services firm seals a five-year, $1.46 billion AI partnership with the German sports car maker alongside the acquisition of its 4,500-employee consulting subsidiary.
body:
• TCS will acquire 100% of Porsche's management and IT consulting subsidiary MHP for €320 million ($373 million) in an all-cash deal expected to close in three to four months.
  • Alongside the acquisition, TCS and Porsche have signed a five-year technology partnership worth €1.25 billion ($1.46 billion) focused on AI-led transformation across manufacturing, engineering, and customer experience.
  • MHP, headquartered in Ludwigsburg, Germany, employs approximately 4,500 people and reported a turnover of €742 million in calendar year 2025.

The Deal

Tata Consultancy Services announced on Monday that its Netherlands subsidiary, Tata Consultancy Services Netherlands B.V., has signed a share purchase agreement to acquire 100% of Porsche AG's management and IT consulting subsidiary, MHP Management- und IT-Beratung GmbH, for an enterprise value of €320 million ($373 million).

https://youtube.com/watch?v=f54pkJ3q1IM

The all-cash acquisition is subject to regulatory approval from the European Commission under EU merger-control and Foreign Subsidies Regulation, foreign investment clearance in Romania, and a certificate of non-objection from Germany's Federal Ministry of Economy and Energy. TCS expects the transaction to close within three to four months.

MHP provides consulting and technology services spanning business consulting, digital transformation, AI, SAP transformation, manufacturing digitalization, connected mobility, and software-defined mobility. It will retain its brand and continue operating as an independent consultancy under TCS ownership.

"Porsche is taking another important step in its strategy to focus resolutely on its core business with the transfer of MHP to Tata Consultancy Services. At the same time, we are gaining a strategic partner in TCS."

— Michael Leiters, CEO, Porsche AG

A $1.46 Billion AI Partnership

Separate from the acquisition, Porsche has committed €1.25 billion ($1.46 billion) over five years to TCS and MHP for AI-led transformation work. Under the agreement, TCS will establish a dedicated AI Mobility Centre of Excellence to develop and scale applications across Porsche's manufacturing, engineering, operations, customer experience, and enterprise functions.

The partnership combines Porsche's automotive engineering and brand expertise with TCS's capabilities in AI, product engineering, and business transformation. The companies said the work will extend to next-generation automotive technology services and software-defined mobility platforms, though neither identified specific first applications or implementation targets.

TCS CEO K. Krithivasan said the partnership positions MHP for global expansion. "Currently, MHP operates only in Europe, and now we are able to operate at a global scale with this combined entity. Porsche will be our customer zero, but our centre will bring solutions to all other automobile customers, expanding the scale and scope of what we can do together," he said.

TCS's Growing Acquisition Streak

The MHP acquisition is TCS's third AI-focused deal in the past year, following the $700 million purchase of U.S.-based multi-cloud consultancy Coastal Cloud and the $72.8 million acquisition of digital marketing and IT consulting firm ListEngage. The three deals signal a deliberate shift toward inorganic growth for TCS, which has historically favored organic expansion.

According to The Hindu BusinessLine, the deal is expected to reduce TCS's operating margins by 50 to 60 basis points over the next four to six quarters. Krithivasan said the company expects to improve margins over time through increased offshore delivery and other operational levers.

Implications for India's IT Sector

The acquisition extends TCS's footprint into European automotive consulting, a market historically dominated by German and Western European firms. For the broader Indian IT services sector, the deal demonstrates the growing willingness of marquee global brands to entrust Indian companies with core consulting and technology functions beyond traditional outsourcing.

Porsche CEO Michael Leiters framed the move as a vote of confidence in TCS's breadth. "We think that MHP is in much better hands in TCS because they have the breadth to extend business opportunities for MHP," he said, adding that the combination of Porsche's automotive expertise and TCS's digital technology capabilities would help the automaker improve innovation and competitiveness as the industry becomes more software-driven.

What's Next

The transaction awaits regulatory approvals across multiple European jurisdictions. Once closed, MHP's 4,500 employees will join TCS's workforce of over 600,000, and the AI Mobility Centre of Excellence will begin developing solutions for Porsche's value chain. The partnership's success will likely be measured by whether TCS can replicate the model with other European automakers and industrial customers in a sector undergoing rapid digital transformation.
